citation: Zhang S, Guo Q, Gai W, Guo Y, Zheng Y. A comprehensive evaluation of plasma metagenomics sequencing for the diagnosis of suspected infection in pediatric patients with hematologic diseases. Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology. 2025;15:1584214.

population.population_description: Children with hematological disorders and suspected early infection who underwent blood mNGS at Anhui Children's Hospital (80 enrolled, 73 analyzed); 66 (90.41%) immunosuppressed mainly by chemotherapy; 64 infected vs 9 non-infected by final clinical diagnosis

neutropenic_status: Not a formal inclusion criterion; neutropenia reported via NE counts (median 0.32x10^9/L); neutropenic patients more likely mNGS-positive

specimens.type: site-directed specimens for CMT (BALF, sputum, CSF, bone marrow, urine, PICC)

index_test.platform_or_panel: Plasma cfDNA mNGS (PathoXtract extraction, KAPA Hyper Prep library, MGISEQ-200, 50 bp single-end; WillingMed Technology Beijing involvement)

reference_standard: Final clinical diagnosis (infected vs non-infected) determined by clinical symptoms, microbial test results, laboratory indexes, imaging features, and clinical treatment response

comparator_2x2.note: This is mNGS-vs-CMT agreement, NOT vs final clinical diagnosis; the mNGS-vs-final-diagnosis 2x2 (infected n=64, non-infected n=9) is not reported numerically. Cells derived from reported percentages: both positive 19/73 (26.03%), both negative 20/73 (27.40%), CMT-only 3/73 (4.11%), mNGS-only 31/73 (42%).

diagnostic_yield.n_positive_relevant_pathogens: mNGS positive 69.86% (51/73) vs CMT 31.51% (23/73) vs blood culture 12.33% (9/73); 46 pathogens detected in infected patients, 34 only by mNGS, 5 only by CMT; 41 pathogens by mNGS vs 12 by CMT
diagnostic_yield.basis: positive detection among 73 patients; infected subgroup n=64

additional_yield_vs_conventional: mNGS-only positives 42% (31/73); CMT-only 4.11% (3/73); among 19 double-positive patients only 4 (21.05%) exactly matched.
therapy_change: mNGS had positive effect on treatment in 65.75% (48/73): antibiotic initiation 8 (10.96%), escalation 11 (15.07%), de-escalation 18 (24.66%), confirmation of empirical treatment 11 (15.07%); no effect 25; negative effect 0
mortality_or_outcomes: Not reported (discharge/death only appears as a no-effect category M6 with 0 cases)

quality_flags.overlap_risk: Single center pediatric; retrospective; mNGS not always on same date; empiric antibiotics before mNGS common

quadas2_notes: Retrospective; final clinical diagnosis used CMT/microbiology and clinical response - incorporation risk; no mNGS-vs-final-diagnosis 2x2 numerically reported (only infected n=64 vs non-infected n=9). No TAT.

evidence_quotes.quote: We retrospectively analyzed the clinical data of 73 children with hematological disorders suspected of early infection admitted to Anhui Children's Hospital between September 2023 and February 2024.
The positive rate of mNGS was significantly higher than that of CMT (69.86% vs 31.51%
In patients with hematologic disease, the positive rate of plasma mNGS was significantly higher than that of BC (69.86% vs 12.33%

26.03% (19/73) of patients were positive for both mNGS and CMT. 27.40% (20/73) of patients were negative. Positive pathogens were acquired by CMT alone in 4.11% (3/73) of patients and positive pathogens by plasma mNGS only in 42% of patients.

They were classified into infected (n=64) and non-infected groups (n=9) based on their final clinical diagnosis, which was mainly determined by clinical symptoms, microbial test results, laboratory indexes, imaging features, and clinical treatment.
A total of 46 pathogens were detected in all infected patients, of which 34 pathogens were detected only in plasma mNGS. 5 pathogens were detected only by CMT
Among the 73 patients with suspected infection, plasma mNGS had a positive effect on the treatment of 65.75% (48/73) of patients
